questions.title: Meaning of String Immutability
questions.description: Strings in Java are called immutable. What does this property mean?
questions.Option1: Once created, the characters of a String object can never be changed; every modification produces a new String object
questions.Option2: A String cannot be passed as a method parameter
questions.Option3: A String cannot be joined with another String using +
questions.Option4: A String variable cannot be assigned a different value later

questions.title: toUpperCase Returns a New String
questions.description: Given a String s holding abc, what happens after the call s.toUpperCase(); completes?
questions.Option1: It returns a new string ABC and the original string still holds abc
questions.Option2: The string s itself becomes ABC
questions.Option3: The call is a compile-time error because s is immutable

questions.title: Why StringBuilder Is Preferred in Loops
questions.description: Why is StringBuilder usually preferred over String concatenation when building a large text inside a loop?
questions.Option1: StringBuilder stores characters more compactly than String
questions.Option2: String objects are immutable, so each concatenation creates a new object, while StringBuilder modifies its internal character buffer
questions.Option3: String concatenation is forbidden inside loops
